verses.sanskrit:
जनमेजय उवाच।
              किमर्थं द्विजशार्दूलं धर्मराजो युधिष्ठिरः। गान्धार्याः प्रेषयामास वासुदेवं परन्तपम्॥१॥
verses.english: Janamejaya said “Why did that best of kings, viz., the righteous Yudhishthira, send that scorcher of foes, viz., Vasudeva, to Gandhari? Krishna had at first gone to the Kauravas for the sake of bringing about peace. He was not successful. For this the battle took place.

verses.sanskrit: यदा पूर्वं गतः कृष्णः शमार्थं कौरवान्प्रति। न च तं लब्धवान्कामं ततो युद्धमभूदिदम्॥२॥
निहतेषु तु योधेषु हते दुर्योधने तदा। पृथिव्यां पाण्डवेयस्य निःसपत्ने कृते युधि॥३॥
विद्रुते शिबिरे शून्ये प्राप्ते यशसि चोत्तमे। किं न तत्कारणं ब्रह्मन् येन कृष्णो गतः पुनः॥४॥
verses.english: When all the warriors were killed and Duryodhana was struck down, when for the battle the empire of Pandu's son became perfectly safe, when all the (Kuru) camp became empty, when the son of Pandu won great glory, what was the cause for which Krishna had once again to go (to Hastinapura)?

verses.sanskrit: न चैतत्कारपां ब्रह्मन्नल्पं विप्रतिभाति मे। यत्रागमदमेयात्मा स्वयमेव जनार्दनः॥५॥
verses.english: It seems to me, O Brahimana, that the cause could not be an insignificant one, since it was Janarddana had himself to make the journey.

verses.sanskrit: तत्त्वतो वै समाचक्ष्व सर्वमध्वर्युसत्तम। यच्चात्र कारणं ब्रह्मन् कार्यस्यास्य विनिश्चये॥६॥

वैशम्पायन उवाच।
              त्वद्युक्तोऽयमनुप्रश्नो यन्मां पृच्छसि पार्थिव। तत्तेऽहं सम्प्रवक्ष्यामि यथावद्भरतर्षभ॥७॥
verses.english: Vaishampayana said “The question you have put, O king, is, indeed, worthy of you! I will tell you everything truly truly as it happened. See Duryodhana, the powerful son of Dhritarashtra, struck down by Bhimasena against the rule of fair fight, and beholding the Kuru king slain unfairly. O Bharata, Yudhishthira, O monarch, was filled with great fear, thinking of the highly-blessed and ascetic Gandhari-'See has practised severe ascetic austerities and can, therefore, consume the three worlds,' this was the thought of the son of Pandu. By sending Krishna, the angry Gandhari, Gandhari, would be comforted before Yudhishthira's own arrival.

verses.sanskrit: हतं दुर्योधनं दृष्ट्वा भीमसेनेन संयुगे। व्युत्क्रम्य समयं राजन् धार्तराष्ट्रं महाबलम्॥८॥
अन्यायेन हतं दृष्ट्वा गदायुद्धेन भारत। युधिष्ठिरं महाराज महद्भयमथाविशत्॥९॥
चिन्तयानो महाभागं गान्धारीं तपसान्विताम्। घोरेण तपसा युक्तां त्रैलोक्यमपि सा दहेत्॥१०॥
तस्य चिन्तयमानस्य बुद्धिः समभवत्तदा। गान्धार्याः क्रोधदीप्तायाः पूर्वं प्रशमनं भवेत्॥११॥
सा हि पुत्रवधं श्रुत्वा कृतमस्माभिरीदृशम्। मानसेनाग्निना क्रुद्धा भस्मसान्नः करिष्यति॥१२॥
verses.english: Hearing of the death of her son in such a way, she will, in anger, with the fire of her mind, reduce us to ashes.

verses.sanskrit: कथं दुःखमिदं तीव्रं गान्धारी सम्प्रशक्ष्यति। श्रुत्वा विनिहतं पुत्रं छलेनाजिह्मयोधिनम्॥१३॥
एवं विचिन्त्य बहुधा भयशोकसमन्वितः। वासुदेवमिदं वाक्यं धर्मराजोऽभ्यभाषत॥१४॥
verses.english: How will Gandhari bear such poignant grief, after hearing of her son, who always fought fairly, being slain unfairly by us?' Having thought thus for a long while, king Yudhishthira filled with fear and fried said these words to Vasudeva.

verses.sanskrit: तव प्रसादाद्गोविन्द राज्यं निहतकण्टकम्। अप्राप्यं मनसापीदं प्राप्तमस्माभिरच्युत॥१५॥
verses.english: Through your kindness, O Govinda, my kingdom has been freed from pests. We have gained now what we could not even imagine. Omighty-armed one, in battle, making the very hair to stand on end, thou hadst to bear voilent blows before my very eyes, O delighter of the Yadavas.

verses.sanskrit: प्रत्यक्षं मे महाबाहो सङ्ग्रामे लोमहर्षणे। विमर्दः सुमहान्प्राप्तस्त्वया यादवनन्दन॥१६॥
त्वया देवासुरे युद्धे वधार्थममरद्विषाम्। यथा साह्यं पुरा दत्तं हताश्च विबुधद्विषः॥१७॥
verses.english: Formerly in the battle between the gods and। the Asuras, thou hadst, lent your help for the destruction of the foes of the celestials, and those enemies were killed.

verses.sanskrit: साह्यं तथा महाबाहो दत्तमस्माकमच्युत। सारथ्येन च वार्ष्णेय भवता हि धृता वयम्॥१८॥
verses.english: Similarly, O mighty-armed one, you have helped us, O you of unfading glory. By agreeing to act as our charioteer, O Vrishnihero, you have all along protected us.

verses.sanskrit: यदि न त्वं भवेन्नाथः फाल्गुनस्य महारणे। कथं शक्यो रणे जेतुं भवेदेष बलार्णवः॥१९॥
verses.english: If you had not protected Phalguna in dreadful battle, this sea of troops would not have been vanquished?

verses.sanskrit: गदाप्रहारा विपुलाः परिघैश्चापि ताडनम्। शक्तिभिर्भिन्दिपालैश्च तोमरैः सपरश्वधैः॥२०॥
verses.english: You have suffered many blows of the mace, and many strokes of spiked bludgeons and dart and short arrows and lances and battle-axes.

verses.sanskrit: अस्मत्कृते त्वया कृष्ण वाचः सुपरुषाः श्रुताः। शस्त्राणां च निपाता वै वज्रस्पर्शोपमा रणे॥२१॥
ते च ते सफला जाता हते दुर्योधनेऽच्युत। तत्सर्वं न यथा नश्येत्पुनः क्रोधं कृष्ण तथा कुरु॥२२॥
verses.english: On account of Duryodhana's death, all this has not been fruitless, O you of unfading glory. O Krishna, our heart, however, is yet trembling in doubt. Know, O Madhava, that Gandhari's wrath, has been excited.

verses.sanskrit: सन्देहदोलां प्राप्तं नश्चेतः कृष्ण जये सति। गान्धार्या हि महाबाहो क्रोधं बुद्ध्यस्व माधव॥२३॥
सा हि नित्यं महाभाग तपसोग्रेण कर्शिता। पुत्रपौत्रवधं श्रुत्वा ध्रुवं नः सम्प्रधक्ष्यति॥२४॥
verses.english: That highly-blessed lady is always weakening herself with the austerest of penances. Hearing of the death of her sons and grandsons, she will forsooth, reduce us to ashes. It is time, O hero, I think, for pacifying her.

verses.sanskrit: तस्याः प्रसादनं वीर प्राप्तकालं मतं मम। कश्च तां क्रोधताम्राक्षीं पुत्रव्यसनकर्शिताम्॥२५॥
वीक्षितुं पुरुषः शक्तस्त्वामृते पुरुषोत्तम। तत्र मे गमनं प्राप्तं रोचते तव माधव॥२६॥
verses.english: Save you, O foremost of men, what other person is there that can even face that lady of red and ranging eyes and greatly overwhelmed with the misfortunes of her children.

verses.sanskrit: गान्धार्याः क्रोधदीप्तायाः प्रशमार्थमरिन्दम। त्वं हि कर्ता विकर्ता च लोकानां प्रभवाव्ययः॥२७॥
verses.english: O Madhava, I think it is better for you to go, for pacifying Gandhari, O chastiser of foes, who is blazing with wrath. You are the Creator and the Destroyer. You are the first cause of all the worlds, yourself being eternal.

verses.sanskrit: हेतुकारणसंयुक्तैर्वाक्यैः कालसमीरितैः। क्षिप्रमेव महाबाहो गान्धारीं शमयिष्यसि॥२८॥
verses.english: With reasonable words, you will quickly, O you of great wisdomn, be able to pacify Gandhari.

verses.sanskrit: पितामहश्च भगवान् कृष्णस्तत्र भविष्यति। सर्वथा ते महाबाहो गान्धार्याः क्रोधनाशनम्॥२९॥
verses.english: Our grandsire, the holy KrishnaDvaipayana, will be there. O mighty-armed one, it is your duty to remove by all means in thy power, the anger of Gandhari.
verses.bhavadeepa: हेतुकारणसंयुक्तैः हेतवो दृष्टा अपराधाः कारणानि अदृष्टान्यवश्यम्भावीनि तैर्युक्तानि तैः॥२८॥

verses.sanskrit: कर्तव्यं सात्वतां श्रेष्ठ पाण्डवानां हितार्थिना। धर्मराजस्य वचनं श्रुत्वा यदुकुलोद्वहः॥३०॥
आमन्त्र्य दारुकं प्राह रथः सज्जो विधीयताम्। केशवस्य वचः श्रुत्वा त्वरमाणोऽथ दारुकः॥३१॥
verses.english: Hearing these words of king Yudhishthira, the Yadu-hero summoning Daruka, said 'Get may car ready.'

verses.sanskrit: न्यवेदयद्रथं सज्जे केशवाय महात्मने। तं रथं यादवश्रेष्ठः समारुह्य परन्तपः॥३२॥
verses.english: Having received Keshava's command, Daruka speedily returned and represented to his great master that the car was ready.

verses.sanskrit: जगाम हास्तिनपुरं त्वरितः केशवो विभुः। ततः प्रायान्महाराज माधवो भगवान् रथी॥३३॥
verses.english: That destroyer of foes and chief of Yadu's race, viz., the Lord Keshava, having got upon the car, proceeded speedily to the city of the Kurus.

verses.sanskrit: नागसाह्वयमासाद्य प्रविवेश न वीर्यवान्। प्रविश्य नगरं वीरो रथघोषेण नादयन्॥३४॥
verses.english: The worshipful Madhava then, mounting his vehicle, proceeded, and arrived Hastinapur. at

verses.sanskrit: विदितं धृतराष्ट्रस्य सोऽवतीर्य रथोत्तमात्। अभ्यगच्छददीनात्मा धृतराष्ट्रनिवेशनम्॥३५॥
verses.english: Making the city resound with the rattle of his car-wheels as he entered it, he sent word to Dhritarashtra and then got down from his car and entered the palace of the old king.

verses.sanskrit: पूर्वं चाभिगतं तत्र सोऽपश्यदृषिसत्तमम्। पादौ प्रपीड्य कृष्णस्य राज्ञश्चापि जनार्दनः॥३६॥
verses.english: He there saw that best of Rishis, (viz., Dvaipayana), arrived before him. Embracing the feet of both Vyasa and Dhritarashtra, Janarddana quietly saluted Gandhari also. Then the best of the Yadavas, viz., Vishnu, holding Dhritarashtra by the hand, O king, began to weep.

verses.sanskrit: अभ्यवादयदव्यग्रो गान्धारीं चापि केशवः। ततस्तु यादवश्रेष्ठो धृतराष्ट्रमधोक्षजः॥३७॥
पाणिमालम्ब्य राजेन्द्र सुस्वरं प्ररुरोद ह। स मुहूर्तादिवोत्सृज्य बाष्पं शोकसमुद्भवम्॥३८॥
प्रक्षाल्य वारिणा नेत्रे ह्याचम्य च यथाविधि। उवाच प्रस्तुतं वाक्यं धृतराष्ट्रमरिन्दमः॥३९॥
न तेऽस्त्यविदितं किञ्चिद्वृद्धस्य तव भारत। कालस्य च यथावृत्तं तत्ते सुविदितं प्रभो॥४०॥
यदिदं पाण्डवैः सर्वैस्तव चित्तानुरोधिभिः। कथं कुलक्षयो न स्यात्तथा क्षत्रस्य भारत॥४१॥
verses.english: Out of respect for you the Pandavas had tried to prevent the destruction of their family and the extermination of the Kshatriyas, O Bharata.

verses.sanskrit: भ्रातृभिः समयं कृत्वा क्षान्तवान् धर्मवत्सलः। द्यूतच्छलजितैः शुद्धैर्वनवासो ह्युपागतः॥४२॥
verses.english: Having made a compact with his brothers, the virtuous Yudhishthira had lived peacefully. He even went to exile after the unfair defeat at dice.

verses.sanskrit: अज्ञातवासचर्या च नानावेषसमावृतैः। अन्ये च बहवः क्लेशात्स्वशक्तैरिव सर्वदा॥४३॥
verses.english: With his brothers he lived in concealment and disguise. They also suffered various miseries as if they were quite helpless.

verses.sanskrit: मया च स्वयमागम्य युद्धकाल उपस्थिते। सर्वलोकस्य सान्निध्ये ग्रामांस्त्वं पञ्च याचितः॥४४॥
verses.english: On the eve of batile I myself came, and before all begged of you only five villages.

verses.sanskrit: त्वया कालोपसृष्टेन लोभतो नापवर्जिताः। तवापराधान्नृपते सर्वं क्षत्रं क्षयं गतम्॥४५॥
verses.english: Out of covetousness, and as destiny would nave it, you did not grant my request. Through you folly, O king, all the Kshatriyas have been exterminated.

verses.sanskrit: भीष्मेण सोमदत्तेन बाह्लीकेन कृपेण च। द्रोणेन च सपुत्रेण विदुरेण च धीमता॥४६॥
verses.english: Bhisma, and Somadatta, and Valhika, and Kripa, and Drona, and his son and the Wise Vidura, always begged you for peace. You did not, however, follow their advice.

verses.sanskrit: याचितस्त्वं शमं नित्यं न च तत्कृतवानसि। कालोपहतचित्ता हि सर्वे मुह्यन्ति भारत॥४७॥
verses.english: Every one, it seems, loses sense under the influence of Destiny, O Bharata, since even you, O king, as regards this matter, did act so foolishly.

verses.sanskrit: यथा मूढो भवान्पूर्वमस्मिन्नर्थे समुद्यते। किमन्यत्कालयोगाद्धि दिष्टमेव परायणम्॥४८॥
मा च दोषान्महाप्राज्ञ पाण्डवेषु निवेशय। अल्पोऽप्यतिक्रमो नास्ति पाण्डवानां महात्मनाम्॥४९॥
verses.english: What else can it be but the effect of Time? Indeed, Destiny always reigns supreme! Do not, O you of great wisdom, attribute any fault to the Pandavas.

verses.sanskrit: धर्मतो न्यायतश्चैव स्नेहतश्च परन्तप। एतत्सर्वं तु विज्ञाय ह्यात्मदोषकृतं फलम्॥५०॥
verses.english: Judged by the standard of Ethics or reason or affection, the Pandavas have not committed the slightest offense, O scorcher of foes.

verses.sanskrit: असूयां पाण्डुपुत्रेषु न भवान्कर्तुमर्हति। कुलं वंशश्च पिण्डाश्च यच्च पुत्रकृतं फलम्॥५१॥
verses.english: Knowing all this to be the fruit of you own folly, it is proper for you not to entertain any ill felling towards the Pandavas.

verses.sanskrit: गान्धार्यास्तव वै नाथ पाण्डवेषु प्रतिष्ठितम्। त्वं चैव कुरुशार्दूल गान्धारी च यशस्विनी॥५२॥
verses.english: The perpetuity of race, the offering of funeral cake, and every thing else that depends upon offspring, now depend on the Pandavas as regards both yourself and Gandhari.

verses.sanskrit: मा शुचो नरशार्दूल पाण्डवान्प्रति किल्बिषम्। एतत्सर्वमनुध्याय आत्मनश्च व्यतिक्रमम्॥५३॥
verses.english: Both you and the renowned Gandhar also, should not entertain malice towards the Pandavas.

verses.sanskrit: शिवेन पाण्डवान्पाहि नमस्ते भरतर्षभ। जानासि च महाबाहो धर्मराजस्य या त्वयि॥५४॥
verses.english: Thinking of all this, and thinking also of your own sins, cherish good feelings towards the Pandavas. I bow to you, O Bharata chief.

verses.sanskrit: भक्तिर्भरतशार्दूल स्नेहश्चापि स्वभावतः। एतच्च कदनं कृत्वा शत्रूणामपकारिणाम्॥५५॥
verses.english: You know, O mighty armed one, the devotion of king Yudhisthira and his affection towards you.

verses.sanskrit: दह्यते स दिवा रात्रौ न च शर्माधिगच्छति। त्वां चैव नरशार्दूल गान्धारीं च यशस्विनीम्॥५६॥
verses.english: Having caused this destruction of foes that wronged him so, he is burning day and night in grief and does and enjoy peace of mind.

verses.sanskrit: स शोचन्नरशार्दूलः शान्तिं नैवाधिगच्छति। ह्रिया च परयाऽऽविष्टो भवन्तं नाधिगच्छति॥५७॥
verses.english: Grieving for you and for Gandhari, he does not enjoy any happiness.

verses.sanskrit: पुत्रशोकाभिसन्तप्तं बुद्धिव्याकुलतेन्द्रियम्। एवमुक्त्वा महाराज धृतराष्ट्रं यदूत्तमः॥५८॥
verses.english: Out of shame he does not appear before you who are burning with grief on account of your children and whose understanding and senses have been bewildered.'—having said these words to Dhritarashtra, that foremost one Yadu's race, O king, addressed the griefstricken Gandhari in these words of great significance-O daughter of Subala, O you of excellent vows, hear what I say. O auspicious dame, there is no lady like you in world.

verses.sanskrit: उवाच परमं वाक्यं गान्धारीं शोककर्शिताम्। सौबलेयि निबोध त्वं यत्त्वां वक्ष्यामि तच्छृणु॥५९॥
त्वत्समानास्ति लोकेऽस्मिन्नद्य सीमन्तिनी शुभे। जानासि च यथा राज्ञि सभायां मम सन्निधौ॥६०॥
धर्मार्थसहितं वाक्यमुभयोः पक्षयोर्हितम्। उक्तवत्यसि कल्याणि न च ते तनयैः कृतम्॥६१॥
verses.english: You remember, O queen, those just and fair words which you gave utterance to the assembly before me, words that were beneficial to both the parties—but which your sons, ( auspicious lady, did not pay any heed to.

verses.sanskrit: दुर्योधनस्त्वया चोक्तो जयार्थी परुषं वचः। शृणु मूढ वचो मह्यं यतो धर्मस्ततो जयः॥६२॥
verses.english: Duryodhana, who coveted victory was reprimanded by you. You told him then-Listen, O fool, to these eternal words, viz., victory follows righteousness-your words, O princes, have now been fulfilled. Knowing all this, O auspicious lady, do not grieve.

verses.sanskrit: तदिदं समनुप्राप्तं तव वाक्यं नृपात्मजे। एवं विदित्वा कल्याणि मा स्म शोके मनः कृथाः॥६३॥
पाण्डवानां विनाशाय मा ते बुद्धिः कदाचन। शक्ता चासि महाभागे पृथिवीं सचराचराम्॥६४॥
verses.english: Let not your heart be bent towards the destruction of the Pandavas. On account of the power of your penances, you are able, O highly blessed one, to consume with your cyes, burning in anger, the whole Earth with her mobile and immobile creatures.'

verses.sanskrit: चक्षुषा क्रोधदीप्तेन निर्दग्धुं तपसो बलात्। वासुदेववचः श्रुत्वा गान्धारी वाक्यमब्रवीत्॥६५॥
एवमेतन्महाबाहो यथा वदसि केशव। आधिभिर्दह्यमानाया मतिः सञ्चलिता मम॥६६॥
verses.english: Hearing these words of Vasudeva, Gandhari said-'O Keshava, what you say is truel

verses.sanskrit: सा मे व्यवस्थिता श्रुत्वा तव वाक्यं जनार्दन। राज्ञस्त्वन्धस्य वृद्धस्य हतपुत्रस्य केशव॥६७॥
verses.english: My heart, burning in grief, had been unfixed. After hearing what you said, however, that heart, O Janarddana, has been settled.

verses.sanskrit: त्वं गतिः सहितैर्वीरैः पाण्डवैर्द्विपदां वरः। एतावदुक्त्वा वचनं मुखं प्रच्छाद्य वाससा॥६८॥
verses.english: Regarding the blind old king, who had now become childless, O foremost of men, you and the sons of Pandu, are his refuge.'

verses.sanskrit: पुत्रशोकाभिसन्तप्ता गान्धारी प्ररुरोद ह। तत एनां महाबाहुः केशवः शोककर्शिताम्॥६९॥
हेतुकारणसंयुक्तैर्वाक्यैराश्वासयत्प्रभुः। समाश्वास्य च गान्धारी धृतराष्ट्रं च माधवः॥७०॥
verses.english: The mighty-armed lord Keshava then solaced the grief-stricken princess with reasonable words and examples.

verses.sanskrit: द्रौणिसङ्कल्पितं भावमवबुद्ध्यत केशवः। ततस्त्वरित उत्थाय पादौ मूर्घ्ना प्रणम्य च॥७१॥
verses.english: Having comforted Gandhari and Dhritarashtra, Keshava of Madhu's race, came to know the evil that was thought of by Drona's son.

verses.sanskrit: द्वैपायनस्य राजेन्द्र ततः कौरवमब्रवीत्। आपृच्छे त्वां कुरुश्रेष्ठ मा च शोके मनः कृथाः॥७२॥
verses.english: Rising up quickly after worshipping the feet of Vyasa with his head, Keshava, O king, addressed Dhritarashtra, saying, 'I take your leave. O foremost of Kuru's race! Do not grieve. The son of Drona has an evil desire. It is for this that I rise so suddenly.

verses.sanskrit: द्रौणेः पापोऽस्त्यभिप्रायस्तेनास्मि सहसोत्थितः। पाण्डवानां वधे रात्रौ बुद्धिस्तेन प्रदर्शिता॥७३॥
एतच्छ्रुत्वा तु वचनं गान्धार्या सहितोऽब्रवीत्। धृतराष्ट्रो महाबाहुः केशवं केशिसूदनम्॥७४॥
शीघ्रं गच्छ महाबाहो पाण्डवान्परिपालय। भूयस्त्वया समेष्यामि क्षिप्रमेव जनार्दन॥७५॥
प्रायात्ततस्तु त्वरितो दारुकेण सहाच्युतः। वासुदेवे गते राजन् धृतराष्ट्रं जनेश्वरम्॥७६॥
verses.english: See us again soon, O Janarddana!-Then Keshava of unfading glory proceeded with Daruka.

verses.sanskrit: आश्वासयदमेयात्मा व्यासो लोकनमस्कृतः। वासुदेवोऽपि धर्मात्मा कृतकृत्यो जगाम ह॥७७॥
verses.english: After Vasudeva had gone, O king, Vyasa, worshipped of the whole world, began to comfort king Dhritarashtra.

verses.sanskrit: शिबिरं हास्तिनपुराद्दिदृक्षुः पाण्डवान्नृप। आगम्य शिबिरं सोऽभ्यगच्छत पाण्डवान्। तच्च तेभ्यः समाख्याय सहितस्तैः समाहितः॥७८॥
